      "text": "**Outlining the Problem**\n\nI\u0027m now zeroing in on the core issue: frequent crashes in the user\u0027s multiplayer tModLoader world, and the resulting loss of items. This suggests the priority should be stability and data preservation in the troubleshooting process.\n\n\n**Interpreting the Error**\n\nI\u0027ve examined the error log image. The \"Main engine crash\" coupled with the `System.InvalidOperationException` points towards a graphics rendering issue within tModLoader. The stack trace highlights a potential conflict or bug in how a mod handles rendering hooks, which likely causes the error. The tip suggests a targeted approach of disabling mods individually.\n\n\n**Tracing the Code**\n\nI\u0027ve traced the crash through the call stack. The crash occurs within `SpriteBatch.Begin`, a core graphics engine component. The stack reveals that the base game handles drawing the map and heads. Crucially, I see dynamically generated methods likely injected by mods. I\u0027ve pinpointed specific mods involved: Calamity Mod, GravityDontFlipScreen, and HighFPSSupport. They are each hooking into the drawing process.\n\n\n**Pinpointing the Culprit**\n\nI\u0027ve determined the crash is a rendering conflict, specifically a missing `SpriteBatch.End`. The stack trace confirms Calamity Mod, GravityDontFlipScreen, and HighFPSSupport all hook into the main draw loop at the point of the crash. My reasoning is that these mods are likely fighting for rendering priority, or that one has a bug which causes a failure to close a `SpriteBatch`. For immediate relief, I\u0027ll suggest autosave or manual saving. Then I will recommend disabling those mods. I\u0027ll recommend they start with the smaller utility mods.\n\n\n**Prioritizing Mod Conflict**\n\nI\u0027m now focusing on mod conflicts, since it is a crucial area for diagnosis. HighFPS Support is my leading suspect, given its reputation for rendering conflicts, particularly with large mods. GravityDontFlipScreen is another candidate, modifying the rendering process in a similar manner. If targeted fixes fail, I will fall back to binary searches and update checks. I will also make sure to highlight the importance of synchronized mod lists and versions between the host and clients, since this is multiplayer.\n\n\n",

      "text": "I completely understand your frustration. Losing progress and items in Terraria because of random crashes is incredibly annoying. \n\nBased on the error log you provided, I can tell you exactly what is happening and which mods are causing it. \n\n**The Problem:**\nThe error `Begin has been called before calling End` is a graphics rendering crash. It means a mod tried to start drawing something on your screen but forgot to \"close\" its drawing sequence, causing the game\u0027s graphics engine to trip over itself and crash.\n\n**The Culprits:**\nIf you look closely at the middle of the text in your image, you can see the game lists the specific mods that were modifying the graphics right as the crash happened. The mods fighting with each other are:\n\n1.  **HighFPSSupport** (High FPS Support)\n2.  **GravityDontFlipScreen** (Gravity Doesn\u0027t Flip Screen)\n3.  **Calamity Mod**\n\n### How to fix it:\n\nSince you probably don\u0027t want to disable Calamity (as it\u0027s a massive content mod), the crash is almost certainly a conflict between Calamity and one of those two utility mods.\n\n**Step 1: Disable \"High FPS Support\"**\nI highly recommend disabling this mod first. Mods that uncap or force high framerates in Terraria notoriously break the game\u0027s rendering engine and frequently cause this exact `SpriteBatch` crash, especially in multiplayer and when combined with heavy mods like Calamity.\n\n**Step 2: Disable \"Gravity Doesn\u0027t Flip Screen\" (If Step 1 didn\u0027t work)**\nIf disabling the High FPS mod doesn\u0027t stop the crashing, disable the Gravity mod next. Because this mod specifically changes how the screen renders, it is heavily modifying the same graphics code that Calamity uses.\n\n**Step 3: Test in Multiplayer**\nMake sure **both you and the server host** (if you aren\u0027t the host) disable these mods, reload, and try playing again. \n\n### How to stop losing items while you test:\nWhile you are trying to figure out which mod is doing this, I recommend downloading a mod called **\"Auto Save\"** or **\"Helpful Hotkeys\"** (which has a quick-save hotkey). You can set it to save your player data every few minutes so that if a crash *does* happen, you only lose a minute or two of inventory management instead of everything.",

      "text": "It is incredibly frustrating when you fix one thing and the game just finds another way to break. \n\nThe good news is that you **did** do it right. The previous two mods (`HighFPSSupport` and `GravityDontFlipScreen`) are completely gone from this new error log. \n\nThe bad news is that the error has unmasked the final conflict. If you look at the new log, the crash is happening specifically at `MapHeadRenderer.PrepareRenderTarget` and is being intercepted by Calamity Mod\u0027s `RenderTargetPool_DoDrawHook`.\n\n### What this actually means:\nThe game\u0027s graphics engine is crashing the exact moment it tries to draw the little **\"Heads\" (Player icons, Town NPC icons, or Boss icons) on your minimap or fullscreen map**. Because Calamity heavily modifies how the game renders graphics, its code is getting tangled up with the map icons and crashing your game.\n\nSince this is happening in **Multiplayer**, here is exactly how to stop this specific map crash:\n\n**1. The \"Bugged Armor/Vanity\" Issue (Most Likely in Multiplayer)**\nIn modded multiplayer, if you or your friend equips a specific piece of modded armor, vanity item, or pet that has a corrupted or missing \"Map Head\" icon, it will crash the game for anyone who looks at the map or gets near them. \n*   **The Fix:** Have everyone on the server completely unequip their vanity items and put on standard vanilla armor for a few minutes. See if the crashing immediately stops. If it does, one of the items you were wearing is bugged.\n\n**2. Disable other Map or UI Mods**\nCalamity is a \"jealous\" mod when it comes to graphics. If you have any other mods that change the map or UI, they will fight Calamity and cause this `Spritebatch` crash. Check your mod list for, and temporarily disable:\n*   **Boss Checklist** (Notoriously causes Map Head crashes when it tries to draw boss icons on the map alongside Calamity).\n*   **Lan\u0027s Shared Map** (or any mod that shares map exploration).\n*   **Better Zoom** or any Camera modifiers.\n\n**3. Tweak Calamity\u0027s Config**\nIf you don\u0027t have any other map mods, Calamity itself might be tripping over its own feet. \n*   Go to **Settings \u003e Mod Configuration \u003e Calamity Mod**.\n*   Look for settings related to **Boss Health Bars**, **UI changes**, or **Map Icons**, and try toggling them off.\n\n**A temporary band-aid:** Try turning off your minimap entirely (press Tab until it disappears) while you test these fixes. If the game stops crashing while the minimap is hidden, you know 100% for a fact it\u0027s a map-icon bug causing your item loss.",

      "finishReason": "STOP",
      "tokenCount": 614,
      "parts": [{
        "text": "It is incredibly frustrating when you fix one thing and the game just finds another way to break"
      }, {
        "text": ". \n\nThe good news is that you **did** do it right. The previous two mods (`HighFPSSupport"
      }, {
        "text": "` and `GravityDontFlipScreen`) are completely gone from this new error log. \n\nThe bad news is that the"
      }, {
        "text": " error has unmasked the final conflict. If you look at the new log, the crash is happening specifically at `MapHead"
      }, {
        "text": "Renderer.PrepareRenderTarget` and is being intercepted by Calamity Mod\u0027s `RenderTargetPool_DoDrawHook`.\n\n"
      }, {
        "text": "### What this actually means:\nThe game\u0027s graphics engine is crashing the exact moment it tries to draw the little"
      }, {
        "text": " **\"Heads\" (Player icons, Town NPC icons, or Boss icons) on your minimap or fullscreen map**. Because Cal"
      }, {
        "text": "amity heavily modifies how the game renders graphics, its code is getting tangled up with the map icons and crashing your game.\n\nSince"
      }, {
        "text": " this is happening in **Multiplayer**, here is exactly how to stop this specific map crash:\n\n**1. The \""
      }, {
        "text": "Bugged Armor/Vanity\" Issue (Most Likely in Multiplayer)**\nIn modded multiplayer, if you or your friend equips"
      }, {
        "text": " a specific piece of modded armor, vanity item, or pet that has a corrupted or missing \"Map Head\" icon, it"
      }, {
        "text": " will crash the game for anyone who looks at the map or gets near them. \n*   **The Fix:** Have"
      }, {
        "text": " everyone on the server completely unequip their vanity items and put on standard vanilla armor for a few minutes. See if the crashing"
      }, {
        "text": " immediately stops. If it does, one of the items you were wearing is bugged.\n\n**2. Disable other"
      }, {
        "text": " Map or UI Mods**\nCalamity is a \"jealous\" mod when it comes to graphics. If you have any other"
      }, {
        "text": " mods that change the map or UI, they will fight Calamity and cause this `Spritebatch` crash. Check"
      }, {
        "text": " your mod list for, and temporarily disable:\n*   **Boss Checklist** (Notoriously causes Map Head crashes when it"
      }, {
        "text": " tries to draw boss icons on the map alongside Calamity).\n*   **Lan\u0027s Shared Map** ("
      }, {
        "text": "or any mod that shares map exploration).\n*   **Better Zoom** or any Camera modifiers.\n\n**3. T"
      }, {
        "text": "weak Calamity\u0027s Config**\nIf you don\u0027t have any other map mods, Calamity itself might"
      }, {
        "text": " be tripping over its own feet. \n*   Go to **Settings \u003e Mod Configuration \u003e Calamity Mod**."
      }, {
        "text": "\n*   Look for settings related to **Boss Health Bars**, **UI changes**, or **Map Icons**, and try togg"
      }, {
        "text": "ling them off.\n\n**A temporary band-aid:** Try turning off your minimap entirely (press Tab until it disappears) while"
      }, {
        "text": " you test these fixes. If the game stops crashing while the minimap is hidden, you know 100%"
      }, {
        "text": " for a fact it\u0027s a map-icon bug causing your item loss."
      }, {
        "text": "",
        "thoughtSignature": ""
      }]

      "text": "**Investigating Terraria Crash**\n\nI\u0027m currently focused on analyzing the provided `client.log` from the Terraria tModLoader instance. The user reported a recurring \"Begin has been called before calling End\" error, seemingly linked to `MapHeadRenderer` and possibly Calamity mod components in multiplayer. I\u0027m cross-referencing this error message with known tModLoader issues and mod interactions. I\u0027ll need to pinpoint the exact sequence of events leading up to this crash.\n\n\n**Tracing the Exceptions**\n\nI\u0027ve located `System.IndexOutOfRangeException` errors at `05:03:57.829` and `05:03:58.547` in the log. I\u0027m following the stack trace, starting with the `Terraria.Player.GetModPlayer` call, proceeding through `CalamityMod.NPCs.CalamityGlobalNPC`, `InfernumMode.Core.ILEditingStuff`, and ultimately arriving at the drawing of NPCs. It appears the issue stems from an array access violation during NPC drawing, potentially related to Calamity and InfernumMode\u0027s interactions.\n\n\n**Analyzing Drawing Interruption**\n\nI\u0027m now focusing on a `CreditsRollSky.Draw` call, which is intriguing. The stack trace points through `SkyManager`, `DrawSurfaceBG`, and finally arrives at an InfernumMode method. I see this error is silently caught, which makes the problem tricky, as it may not be an immediate crash. It seems the `System.IndexOutOfRangeException` is interrupting the `SpriteBatch` sequence and leaving it in an invalid state. I\u0027m investigating how this orphaned `SpriteBatch` state affects subsequent drawing operations, as a failure during drawing could cause downstream issues.\n\n\n**Pinpointing the SpriteBatch Issue**\n\nI\u0027ve traced the issue to `CreditsRollSky.Draw` which is called during a silent exception. This is particularly insightful. The root cause appears to be the `InfernumMode.Core.ILEditingStuff.OverrideSystemHooks::CalGlobalNPCPredrawDetourMethod` method, wrapping `CalamityGlobalNPC:PreDraw`. Specifically, an exception occurs in `InfernumMode.Core.ILEditingStuff.DrawVoidBackgroundDuringMLFightHook.PrepareShaderForBG`. It looks like Infernum is trying to draw the Void background during an interesting sequence. Crucially, the corrupted SpriteBatch state then leads to the crash we see with the `MapHeadRenderer` and the \"Begin has been called before calling End\" error. Now, the question is what\u0027s the correct order of operations, and why is this occurring?\n\n\n**Connecting Multiplayer \u0026 Crash**\n\nI\u0027m now zeroing in on the multiplayer aspect. It appears the crash stems from `CreditsRollSky` being invoked, likely related to InfernumMode and CalamityMod, specifically during the title screen or credits. The error might relate to a bug with Infernum and Calamity in multiplayer where background/sky or NPC drawing fails, and a `DrawSurfaceBG` call is made. I suspect an invalid player index is accessed, likely in the main menu/credits.\n\n\n**Confirming Infernum Conflict**\n\nI\u0027m now certain InfernumMode\u0027s background drawing hooks are the core issue. I\u0027ve re-examined the loaded mods. It\u0027s clear: Infernum\u0027s background drawing hooks cause crashes due to a invalid player index. It seems to be triggered by `CreditsRollSky` during title screens, where `InfernumMode` attempts background processing, ultimately failing due to CalamityMod\u0027s interaction, causing the `IndexOutOfRangeException`. This is exacerbated by the `InfernumMultiplayerPatch`.\n\n\n**Clarifying the Root Cause**\n\nI\u0027ve realized the crash isn\u0027t directly related to the `MapHeadRenderer`. It\u0027s a symptom, not the cause. A silent exception during drawing in `InfernumMode` breaks the `SpriteBatch`. Since it\u0027s caught, the `SpriteBatch.End()` call is skipped, and later the game crashes when drawing the map. It\u0027s Infernum\u0027s interaction with Calamity\u0027s drawing code that results in the silent exception. This is likely during a custom background draw, such as the Moon Lord void background.\n\n\n**Formulating the Fix**\n\nI\u0027ve got a clearer picture: an out-of-bounds player index leads to the `IndexOutOfRangeException` within `Player.GetModPlayer`, which is being caused by `InfernumMode.Core.ILEditingStuff.DrawVoidBackgroundDuringMLFightHook`. It seems highly likely the problem lies in InfernumMode and its interaction with Moon Lord-related triggers, particularly in a multiplayer environment. My next step will be to explore how to best advise the user. I\u0027ll recommend they try disabling InfernumMode.\n\n\n",

      "text": "This log file is exactly what we needed. We finally have the smoking gun, and it proves that the game was actually lying to us in those error screenshots. \n\nThe `MapHeadRenderer` crash you were seeing was a **red herring**. It was the *victim*, not the cause.\n\n### The Real Culprit: Infernum Mode (and a silent crash)\n\nIf you scroll to the very bottom of the text you just pasted, you\u0027ll see a `Silently Caught Exception` happening repeatedly right before the game dies:\n`at InfernumMode.Core.ILEditingStuff.DrawVoidBackgroundDuringMLFightHook.PrepareShaderForBG`\n`at InfernumMode...CalGlobalNPCPredrawDetourMethod`\n\n**Here is exactly what is happening behind the scenes:**\n1. **Infernum Mode** is trying to draw a custom background effect (the code specifically mentions the Moon Lord \"Void Background\" or the Credits sky).\n2. While drawing this background, Infernum tells **Calamity Mod** to draw an NPC. \n3. Calamity tries to check a Player\u0027s stats to see how it should draw the NPC... but because you are in Multiplayer, a slight connection desync causes it to look for a Player that isn\u0027t currently loaded.\n4. This causes a silent `IndexOutOfRangeException` (an invisible crash). \n5. Because the game \"crashed\" in the middle of drawing the background, it **forgot to turn off its drawing tool** (it never called `SpriteBatch.End`).\n6. A microsecond later, the game tries to draw your Minimap. It tries to turn on the drawing tool, realizes the tool is *already* turned on and broken from Infernum\u0027s silent crash, and **fatally crashes your entire game.**\n\n### How to fix it:\n\nThe crash is directly tied to **Infernum Mode** failing to render graphics properly in a multiplayer environment. \n\n**Step 1: The \"Moon Lord / Void\" Trigger**\nThe code specifically mentions `DrawVoidBackgroundDuringMLFightHook`. \n* Are you or your friends currently fighting the Moon Lord?\n* Did someone just equip a Moon Lord pet, relic, or vanity item that might be tricking the game into thinking the Moon Lord background should be active?\n* Did someone just beat the game and trigger the Credits roll? \nWhatever is causing that specific background to try and load is your immediate trigger. Have everyone take off their pets/vanity to see if it stops.\n\n**Step 2: Disable Infernum Mode (The hard truth)**\nI see you have the `InfernumMultiplayerPatch` installed. The harsh reality of modded Terraria is that **Infernum Mode is notoriously broken in multiplayer.** Even with patches, its custom boss AIs and heavy graphical background changes constantly cause desyncs and `SpriteBatch` crashes like the one you are experiencing. \n* If you want to stop losing your items, you will likely need to disable **Infernum Mode** and the **Infernum Multiplayer Patch** and play standard Calamity Death/Revengeance mode. \n\n**Step 3: A potential setting fix (If you refuse to disable Infernum)**\nIf you absolutely *must* play Infernum, you might be able to stop the crash by disabling its custom backgrounds.\n* Go to **Settings \u003e Mod Configuration \u003e Infernum Mode**.\n* Look for settings related to **Custom Boss Backgrounds**, **Void Skies**, or **Screen Shaders**.         "text": ", relic, or vanity item that might be tricking the game into thinking the Moon Lord background should be active?\n*"
      }, {
        "text": " Did someone just beat the game and trigger the Credits roll? \nWhatever is causing that specific background to try and load is your"
      }, {
        "text": " immediate trigger. Have everyone take off their pets/vanity to see if it stops.\n\n**Step 2:"
      }, {
        "text": " Disable Infernum Mode (The hard truth)**\nI see you have the `InfernumMultiplayerPatch` installed."
      }, {
        "text": " The harsh reality of modded Terraria is that **Infernum Mode is notoriously broken in multiplayer.** Even with patches, its"
      }, {
        "text": " custom boss AIs and heavy graphical background changes constantly cause desyncs and `SpriteBatch` crashes like the one you"
      }, {
        "text": " are experiencing. \n* If you want to stop losing your items, you will likely need to disable **Infernum Mode**"
      }, {
        "text": " and the **Infernum Multiplayer Patch** and play standard Calamity Death/Revengeance mode. \n\n**Step "
      }, {
        "text": "3: A potential setting fix (If you refuse to disable Infernum)**\nIf you absolutely *must* play Infer"
      }, {
        "text": "num, you might be able to stop the crash by disabling its custom backgrounds.\n* Go to **Settings \u003e Mod Configuration"
      }, {
        "text": " \u003e Infernum Mode**.\n* Look for settings related to **Custom Boss Backgrounds**, **Void Skies**, or **Screen"
      }, {
        "text": " Shaders**. Turn them all **OFF**. This will prevent Infernum from trying to draw the buggy background that is causing"
      }, {
        "text": " the invisible crash."
